You are a Humanoid.; Size. You are Medium. Many Deorbasuns stand between six and nine feet tall, but your playable size remains Medium.; Speed. Your base walking speed is 35 feet.; Predatory Natural Weapons. Your claws, fangs, talons, horns, or tail are natural weapons. When you hit with an unarmed strike, you may deal slashing, piercing, or bludgeoning damage equal to 1d6 + your Strength or Dexterity modifier.; Soul-Animal Instinct. Choose one instinct when selecting this race: Hunter, Guardian, Winged, Venomtail, or Mystic. Hunter grants proficiency in Stealth or Survival. Guardian grants proficiency in Intimidation or Athletics. Winged grants the Winged Maneuver trait below. Venomtail lets your natural weapon deal poison damage instead of its normal type once per turn. Mystic grants proficiency in Arcana, Nature, or Religion.; Ritual Hunt. Once per long rest, as a bonus action, you mark one creature you can see for 1 minute. The first time each turn you hit the marked creature with an attack, you deal extra damage equal to your proficiency bonus. This damage type matches your natural weapon or a magical energy associated with your soul-animal.; Winged Maneuver. If you chose the Winged instinct, your wings allow brief aerial control. When you jump or fall, you may glide up to 20 feet horizontally and reduce falling damage by an amount equal to five times your level.; Territorial Awareness. You have advantage on Wisdom (Perception or Survival) checks made to track creatures, sense intruders, identify disturbed terrain, or notice magical disturbances in your claimed territory or current campsite.; Languages. You can speak, read, and write Common and one additional language of your choice.

Wings, tails, or subtle soul-animal traits enhance both presence and ability, with wings capable of flight or generating gusts, tails delivering venom, radiant energy, or prehensile utility, and faint ethereal markings or patterns tying form to instinct and magic. Deorbasuns possess extraordinary physical and magical abilities that blend predatory skill, shapeshifting versatility, and environmental attunement. They can leap with precision, maneuver through air or terrain with grace, and strike with claws, fangs, or tails imbued with energy or venom. Some can shift subtly to reflect traits of a soul-animal, such as enhanced senses, agility, or elemental affinities, while others maintain a consistently imposing, feline-like or beastly form. Their endurance and stamina are exceptional, allowing them to traverse rugged terrain, hunt, or perform ritualized movement for extended periods. They absorb energy through magical currents, prey, or ambient mana, and their focus and vitality are renewed through hunting, meditation, ritual exposure, or communion with natural and mystical environments. Deorbasuns are highly perceptive, capable of reading subtle environmental cues, sensing magical disturbances, and coordinating with wildlife or allies in ways that reflect both strategic intelligence and instinctual response.
raceAlignmentDefaults.pantheonInfluence: Creator God: Iskareth. Iskareth is the primary creator of the Deorbasun, shaping their beast-souled bodies from instinct, fertility, natural kinship, and guardian grace. Their soul-animal traits are understood as divine fragments of Iskareth's first wilderness memory: claw, wing, fang, horn, hide, and watchful eye each represent a sacred duty to defend territory without severing kinship with the living world. Secondary Divine Pressures. Anubaldir is honored by territorial guardians who treat endurance and burden as inherited obligations rather than personal virtues. Asethyr influences revels, hunt-feasts, and tribal rites where wilderness freedom becomes sacred survival. Nebyrr appears in boundary law, marriage bonds between guardian clans, and formal oaths that decide who may pass through protected territory. Sigrananna is invoked by moonlit forest Deorbasun, especially those who guard elven groves, old roads, or sacred beasts. Rites, Taboos, and Ichor Marks. The Boundary Vigil sends young Deorbasun to walk the edge of a chosen territory for one full night without speaking, learning where duty ends and domination begins. The First Hunt is not a kill-trial, but a restraint-trial: the initiate must prove they can track, judge, and spare when the land does not require blood. Wasting prey, abandoning a sworn boundary, or hunting only for vanity are deep taboos. Ichor-touched Deorbasun may show glowing paw-print markings, stone-heavy bones, prophetic animal dreams, or a voice that quiets frightened beasts. DM Hooks. Their divine culture supports shrine guardians, border wardens, sacred beast judges, territorial paladins, cursed exiles, or clans divided between Iskareth's kinship and Enkirael's domination. A Deorbasun antagonist does not need to be evil: they may simply believe the party has crossed a boundary the gods themselves once marked.

raceAlignmentDefaults.name: Dril'thar — Grassland Lineage
raceAlignmentDefaults.creatorDominion: Ancient mother of tides, reefs, hidden waters, and oceanic civilizations.
raceAlignmentDefaults.description: Rain-fed grassland and hidden wetland Dril'thar suited to plains, prairie waterholes, and seasonal pools.
raceAlignmentDefaults.lore: The Dril'thar are an ancient amphibious people whose civilizations rise from swamps, flooded jungles, coral reefs, mangrove coasts, subterranean rivers, mist-choked marshes, and sacred rainforests. Across countless regions of the world, they are known as healers, navigators, mystics, hunters, survivalists, and wandering pilgrims capable of thriving where most civilizations would collapse. To outsiders, Dril'thar are often misunderstood as poisonous frogfolk, territorial swamp-creatures, or eerie marsh spirits. In truth, they are one of the most biologically adaptable and spiritually complex peoples in existence. Their philosophy teaches that all things move in cycles: rain becomes river, river becomes sea, decay becomes renewal, and death feeds life anew. Water is not merely an element to the Dril'thar—it is memory, ancestry, spirit, and destiny itself. A spawning pool may serve simultaneously as temple, cemetery, and place of prophecy, for the Dril'thar believe the currents of the world carry the echoes of those who came before.
raceAlignmentDefaults.pantheonInfluence: Creator God: Bastveig. Bastveig is the primary creator of the Dril'thar, binding amphibious mysticism, reef stewardship, hydromancy, and living water memory into their bodies. Dril'thar spawning pools are not only places of birth, but divine archives: their water is believed to remember every ancestor, every flood, every drowning, and every bargain made with the deep. Secondary Divine Pressures. Thoryn-Rahek appears in mutation myths, especially among lineages whose bodies adapt too quickly or in ways that feel alien even to other Dril'thar. Hathruna shapes marsh, rot, and renewal traditions where decay feeds pools and pools feed new life. Horundar influences ocean, storm, and flood clans who believe catastrophe can purify stagnant civilizations. Nefarokir is present in gravewater rites, where pools serve as cemeteries, memory wells, and thresholds for souls who died in water. Lineage Influence Notes. Grassland Dril'thar often honor Ishtanora for rain-fed survival and hidden wetland gardens. Swamp and marsh lineages commonly invoke Hathruna and Nefarokir together, treating rot and death as two halves of the same sacred current. Rainforest and forest lineages add Sigrananna to Bastveig's rites, while reef and ocean lineages are the most direct inheritors of Bastveig's deep-water civilization. Mutated or unusually colored children may be protected, feared, or consecrated depending on whether the clan reads the sign as Bastveig's blessing or Thoryn-Rahek's echo. Rites, Taboos, and Ichor Marks. The Pool of Names ceremony lets a clan recite its dead into living water so the next generation can dream them. The Tide Confession requires a Dril'thar to speak secrets into flowing water rather than into stone, because stillness traps guilt. Polluting a birth-pool, damming ancestral water without consent, or draining a cemetery-marsh are treated as sacrilege. Ichor-touched Dril'thar may develop black bioluminescent freckles, prophetic mucus patterns, voices that ripple water, or mutations that bloom after divine dreams.

raceAlignmentDefaults.pantheonInfluence: Creator God: Bastveig. Bastveig is the primary creator of the Dril'thar, binding amphibious mysticism, reef stewardship, hydromancy, and living water memory into their bodies. Dril'thar spawning pools are not only places of birth, but divine archives: their water is believed to remember every ancestor, every flood, every drowning, and every bargain made with the deep. Secondary Divine Pressures. Thoryn-Rahek appears in mutation myths, especially among lineages whose bodies adapt too quickly or in ways that feel alien even to other Dril'thar. Hathruna shapes marsh, rot, and renewal traditions where decay feeds pools and pools feed new life. Horundar influences ocean, storm, and flood clans who believe catastrophe can purify stagnant civilizations. Nefarokir is present in gravewater rites, where pools serve as cemeteries, memory wells, and thresholds for souls who died in water. Lineage Influence Notes. Swamp and marsh lineages commonly invoke Hathruna and Nefarokir together, treating rot and death as two halves of the same sacred current. Rainforest and forest lineages add Sigrananna to Bastveig's rites, while reef and ocean lineages are the most direct inheritors of Bastveig's deep-water civilization. Mutated or unusually colored children may be protected, feared, or consecrated depending on whether the clan reads the sign as Bastveig's blessing or Thoryn-Rahek's echo. Polluting a birth-pool, damming ancestral water without consent, or draining a cemetery-marsh are treated as sacrilege. Ichor-touched Dril'thar may develop black bioluminescent freckles, prophetic mucus patterns, voices that ripple water, or mutations that bloom after divine dreams.

profileArchetypes.name: Lawful Renegade
profileArchetypes.description: A rebel in legal robes. They bend laws to suit their gain while pretending to be team players - calculating, efficient, and just manipulative enough to get ahead.

profileArchetypes.name: Lawful Drifter
profileArchetypes.description: Follows the rules just enough to survive. Doesn't stick around long, but won't burn bridges either. A ghost with a code.

profileArchetypes.name: Lawful Champion
profileArchetypes.description: Seeks glory under the banner of law. Noble in words, loyal to allies - yet always with an eye on personal legacy.

profileArchetypes.name: Lawful Strategist
profileArchetypes.description: A master planner of the long game. Coldly loyal, ruthlessly efficient, and always thinking ten steps ahead.

profileArchetypes.name: Lawful Knave
profileArchetypes.description: Keeps just enough law to stay out of jail. A slippery operator who toes the line without any deeper loyalties.

profileArchetypes.name: Lawful Avenger
profileArchetypes.description: Enforces personal justice like a holy wrathblade. Rules are tools, not ideals - they punish to feed their pride.

profileArchetypes.name: Lawful Mercenary
profileArchetypes.description: A sword for hire with contracts tattooed on their soul. Lawful only when paid, but never sloppy.

profileArchetypes.name: Lawful Marauder
profileArchetypes.description: Wears structure like armor while carving a bloody path. Not cruel - just committed to their own violent climb.

profileArchetypes.name: Lawful Gladiator
profileArchetypes.description: Upholds combat as ceremony. Respects tradition and fair fights - but glory and personal honor always come first.

profileArchetypes.name: Neutral Renegade
profileArchetypes.description: Works with others only when needed. Often a necessary evil in group efforts - smart, ruthless, and tolerated.

profileArchetypes.name: Neutral Drifter
profileArchetypes.description: A wanderer with just enough charm to stay welcome. Avoids attachment but doesn't actively sabotage it.

profileArchetypes.name: Neutral Champion
profileArchetypes.description: Fights for group causes - until the applause fades. Their heroism is real... but so is their thirst for praise.

profileArchetypes.name: Neutral Strategist
profileArchetypes.description: Thinks only in outcomes, not morals. Moves quietly, makes power plays, and always walks away with more.

profileArchetypes.name: Neutral Knave
profileArchetypes.description: A wildcard with no compass. Acts on impulse or opportunity - sometimes helpful, often a headache.

profileArchetypes.name: Neutral Avenger
profileArchetypes.description: Revenge is their religion. Morality isn’t the goal - just evening the score, no matter who gets in the way.

profileArchetypes.name: Neutral Mercenary
profileArchetypes.description: No gods. No masters. Just coin and contract. Brutal, blunt, and fiercely independent in battle.

profileArchetypes.name: Neutral Marauder
profileArchetypes.description: Fights not for principle, but power. They don’t pick sides - only targets.

profileArchetypes.name: Neutral Gladiator
profileArchetypes.description: Honors the duel, not the war. Cares deeply about reputation and performance, not cause or creed.

profileArchetypes.name: Chaotic Renegade
profileArchetypes.description: A team-friendly anarchist with their own goals. Helps the group... until they don’t.

profileArchetypes.name: Chaotic Drifter
profileArchetypes.description: A storm with a smile. Allies when it’s fun, disappears when it’s not. Hard to hate - but harder to trust.

profileArchetypes.name: Chaotic Champion
profileArchetypes.description: A rebel hero - dramatic, bold, magnetic. Loyal in the moment, but always the star of their own tale.

profileArchetypes.name: Chaotic Strategist
profileArchetypes.description: Unpredictable mastermind. Seeks chaos only they understand, playing both sides to win.

profileArchetypes.name: Chaotic Knave
profileArchetypes.description: Pure mischief incarnate. Chaos is its own reward - no loyalty, no plan, just vibes.

profileArchetypes.name: Chaotic Avenger
profileArchetypes.description: Burns worlds to avenge one wound. Justice isn’t blind - it’s furious.

profileArchetypes.name: Chaotic Mercenary
profileArchetypes.description: A volatile warrior for hire. May switch sides mid-fight if the pay’s better or the thrill is stronger.

profileArchetypes.name: Chaotic Marauder
profileArchetypes.description: Wrecks, raids, and rages with zero remorse. No ideology - just destruction.

profileArchetypes.name: Chaotic Gladiator
profileArchetypes.description: Fights like it’s performance art. Theatrics, blood, and brutal showdowns define them.

profileArchetypes.name: Neutral Operator
profileArchetypes.description: A practical team player. Gets things done with minimal drama and maximum efficiency. Doesn’t care about glory - just results.

profileArchetypes.name: Neutral Collaborator
profileArchetypes.description: Goes with the flow. A team member who supports without leading or resisting - blends in, stabilizes chaos.

profileArchetypes.name: Neutral Harmonizer
profileArchetypes.description: Balances relationships with grace. A quiet peacemaker, not for recognition, but because harmony matters.

profileArchetypes.name: Neutral Adapter
profileArchetypes.description: A true survivalist. Adjusts to any situation without strong ties or ideals. The embodiment of flexible neutrality.

profileArchetypes.name: Neutral Ethicist
profileArchetypes.description: A quiet moral compass. Doesn’t preach, but always chooses the path that harms the fewest - even in stillness.

profileArchetypes.name: Neutral Ravager
profileArchetypes.description: Battles only when needed. Efficient, deadly, and never dramatic. Violence is just another tool.

profileArchetypes.name: Neutral Scoundrel
profileArchetypes.description: A fighter without a cause. May brawl for coin, pride, or boredom - but rarely cares who wins the war.

profileArchetypes.name: Neutral Warrior
profileArchetypes.description: Wields strength as its own code. Neutral in belief, yet bound by a personal oath of fair combat and protection.

profileArchetypes.name: Lawful Coordinator
profileArchetypes.description: A mission-first peacemaker. Brings order and aid to the many, solving problems with a balanced, sensible hand.

profileArchetypes.name: Lawful Mediator
profileArchetypes.description: A fair voice in the storm. Listens before acting, judges without ego, and restores peace without personal gain.

profileArchetypes.name: Lawful Guardian
profileArchetypes.description: The steadfast protector of the realm. Uplifts the weak, obeys the law, and inspires trust with every step.

profileArchetypes.name: Lawful Defender
profileArchetypes.description: A shield with purpose. Puts others first, but doesn’t waste time with idealism. Efficiently defends what matters.

profileArchetypes.name: Lawful Arbiter
profileArchetypes.description: Seeks justice without bias. Mediates with detachment, but never loses sight of the greater good.

profileArchetypes.name: Lawful Sentinel
profileArchetypes.description: The silent watcher. Their loyalty is unwavering, their purpose pure - they serve to protect, not to be seen.

profileArchetypes.name: Lawful Enforcer
profileArchetypes.description: Justice with an edge. Enforces order for the benefit of all - even if it means breaking bones to preserve peace.

profileArchetypes.name: Lawful Vigilante
profileArchetypes.description: Operates in shadows for the light. Defends the helpless but trusts fists over courts. A silent justice.

profileArchetypes.name: Lawful Crusader
profileArchetypes.description: A warrior of divine duty. Law and mercy guide their blade. Fights not for conquest - but for righteousness.

profileArchetypes.name: Neutral Coordinator
profileArchetypes.description: Helps where help is needed. Doesn’t seek control, just solutions. A reliable team lead who lifts others quietly.

profileArchetypes.name: Neutral Mediator
profileArchetypes.description: A calming presence. Bridges gaps between factions, friends, and foes alike. Emotionally grounded and peaceful.

profileArchetypes.name: Neutral Guardian
profileArchetypes.description: The quiet heart of the group. Protects without ego, speaks with compassion, and walks the path of kindness.

profileArchetypes.name: Neutral Defender
profileArchetypes.description: Prioritizes safety over ideology. May not preach morality, but their actions guard the innocent.

profileArchetypes.name: Neutral Arbiter
profileArchetypes.description: A watcher of balance and need. Neither law-bound nor wild, this figure serves the people - however that must look.

profileArchetypes.name: Neutral Sentinel
profileArchetypes.description: Honors a code of protection and patience. Acts when needed, guards without words, and never asks for praise.

profileArchetypes.name: Neutral Enforcer
profileArchetypes.description: Punches through problems so others don’t have to. Brutal, efficient, but undeniably selfless.

profileArchetypes.name: Neutral Vigilante
profileArchetypes.description: Stalks the wicked to defend the helpless. Walks the line between justice and vengeance.

profileArchetypes.name: Neutral Crusader
profileArchetypes.description: Champions the cause without borders. Fights for those who cannot, loyal only to their personal sense of good.

profileArchetypes.name: Chaotic Coordinator
profileArchetypes.description: Leads with heart and improvisation. Makes peace in wild ways - might build a shelter and overthrow the mayor.

profileArchetypes.name: Chaotic Mediator
profileArchetypes.description: The unconventional diplomat. Defuses tension with surprise hugs, strange jokes, or unexpected wisdom.

profileArchetypes.name: Chaotic Guardian
profileArchetypes.description: A wild protector with a golden heart. Thinks laws are optional, but kindness is sacred.

profileArchetypes.name: Chaotic Defender
profileArchetypes.description: Brings safety through unexpected means. May cause a little chaos to save a lot of lives.

profileArchetypes.name: Chaotic Arbiter
profileArchetypes.description: A whimsical judge of right and wrong. Morals fluid, heart steady - they fight for people, not systems.

profileArchetypes.name: Chaotic Sentinel
profileArchetypes.description: Fights with passion and principle. Disregards rules - but never their personal honor.

profileArchetypes.name: Chaotic Enforcer
profileArchetypes.description: Punches down walls to lift people up. Violent but well-meaning - a wrecking ball for good.

profileArchetypes.name: Chaotic Vigilante
profileArchetypes.description: A storm of justice. Protects others even when it means crossing lines, breaking rules, or being feared.

profileArchetypes.name: Chaotic Crusader
profileArchetypes.description: A freedom fighter wrapped in fire. Wields chaos in service of compassion. Unpredictable, unwavering.

races.label: Kaluseban — Arcane Bloodline
races.description: Arcane Kaluseban read ley currents as pattern and beauty, favoring libraries, academies, ritual sites, and strong magical infrastructure.
races.lore: Kalusebans are an elegant and enigmatic race of magical humanoids . They are tall and slender, with graceful features and skin tones that reflect their bloodline, ranging from pale ivory to deep sapphire or earthy greens and browns. Their eyes often glow faintly, carrying hues tied to their magical affinity, and their hair can shimmer, float slightly, or reflect celestial or natural motifs. Kalusebans carry an aura of otherworldly presence, appearing almost ethereal as if the ambient magic bends subtly around them. They thrive in environments rich with mana, nature, or celestial energy, and their forms are highly sensitive to ritual, lunar phases, and environmental harmony. Kalusebans require periodic exposure to magical energy, whether through ley lines, enchanted sites, or ceremonial practices, to maintain their vitality and arcane strength. They bond strongly with natural environments, finding balance and clarity among forests, rivers, or sacred groves. Rituals, music, meditation, or alignment with celestial bodies enhance their mental and emotional equilibrium. Deprivation from magic, polluted areas, or urban confines can weaken their vitality, induce restlessness, or diminish their magical attunement. They also maintain basic needs like nutrition, hydration, and hygiene, often observing these through symbolic or ceremonial acts that reinforce cultural traditions. Kalusebans have abilities tied to their bloodline and affinity. They can manipulate natural or arcane energies, commune with flora and fauna, sense ley lines or currents of magical energy, and subtly influence the environment around them.
races.pantheonInfluence: Creator God: Sigrananna. Sigrananna is the primary creator of the Kaluseban, shaping their ley-line grace, moonlit nature, and shadow-touched elegance from wilderness beauty and lunar power. Kaluseban bodies are often described as living ley-script: skin, eyes, hair, and bloodline traits reveal how moonlight, forest memory, and ambient magic wrote themselves into mortal form. Secondary Divine Pressures. Eirzunet haunts umbral bloodlines, forbidden transformations, cursecraft, and twilight bargains. Bastveig influences Tideborn Kaluseban who listen to reef, river, mist, and rain as extensions of living water memory. Horundar shapes Stonebound and storm-touched lines through pressure, earthquake, weather, and elemental endurance. Raeshkul is honored by arcane scholars who map ley currents as thought-patterns, while Thalunesh appears in dream rites and wandering moonlit pilgrimages. Bloodline Influence Notes. Arcane Kaluseban tend to frame Raeshkul and Sigrananna as paired forces: pattern and beauty. Starborne lines often add Sokhivar's prophecy and distant light. Wildroot lines belong most clearly to Sigrananna's forests, while Tideborn lines blend Sigrananna with Bastveig. Stonebound lines may honor Horundar or Anubaldir depending on whether they read stone as force or burden. Umbral Kaluseban are the most likely to carry Eirzunet's dangerous inheritance. Rites, Taboos, and Ichor Marks. The Moonroot Vigil is a night-long meditation at a ley crossing, where a Kaluseban listens for which god's hunger is nearest to their bloodline. Polluting a ley line, binding a grove without consent, or using beauty to hide predation are serious taboos. Ichor-touched Kaluseban may cast two shadows, glow under moonless skies, hear roots speaking in old languages, or develop silver-black veins that flare during eclipses.

races.label: Geisamahi
races.description: Small Ferretfolk Tinkerers, Scouts, and Clever Problem-Solvers. Bloodlines / Lineages: Geisamahi (ferretfolk tinkerers, scouts, awakened mechanists, adaptive builders)
races.lore: The Geisamahis are small, agile creatures . They resemble large ferrets or stoats but walk upright and possess opposable thumbs, allowing them to manipulate objects with precision. Their bodies are wiry and compact, built for speed, nimbleness, and the ability to navigate tight spaces, while their elongated snouts, expressive eyes, and twitching whiskers reflect their alertness and curiosity. Fur varies in earthy browns, fiery oranges, and snowy whites, often with individualized patterns, and many adorn themselves with small tools, belts, and pouches containing gadgets or relics. They are highly adaptable, thriving in forests, ruins, urban alleys, or other cluttered or complex environments, and they maintain mental sharpness through exploration, invention, and playful problem-solving. Geisamahis have heightened senses and dexterity, allowing them to detect hidden passages, traps, or valuable items that others might miss. They are quick learners and excel at crafting devices, tools, and improvised mechanisms to aid in survival or exploration. Their movements are fluid and acrobatic, capable of extended jumps, climbing, and rapid dashes, enabling them to evade danger or reach otherwise inaccessible areas. They possess a natural instinct for teamwork, often coordinating with kin or allies in subtle, synchronized ways. Their energy and vitality are maintained through frequent rest, light, energy-rich meals, and exposure to natural environments. Geisamahis exhibit keen awareness of their surroundings, sensing traps, subtle hazards, or changes in terrain that might threaten their safety. Their small stature and nimble frame allow them to slip unnoticed through gaps or under cover, and their reflexes enable rapid reactions to threats.
races.pantheonInfluence: Creator God: Marduthor. Marduthor is the primary creator of the Geisamahi, blessing their small ferretfolk hands with tinkering genius, scouting precision, clever repair instincts, and tool-minded problem solving. Many Geisamahi believe the first tool was not a hammer, but a hiding place: invention began when small people learned to survive inside the cracks of large empires. Secondary Divine Pressures. Setrimir is revered by inventors who build devices whose purpose may outgrow their maker. Oskar'enlil studies Geisamahi adaptability as evidence that civilization can evolve through pressure, constraint, and structured experimentation. Nebyrr influences guild charters, apprenticeship contracts, and workshop inheritance, while Ishtanora is honored in burrow-homes where practical inventions protect family, food stores, and community comfort. Rites, Taboos, and Ichor Marks. The First Fixed Thing is the rite of adulthood: a young Geisamahi must repair or improve something useful to the whole burrow. The Gearwake is a memorial where a dead inventor's unfinished designs are distributed to friends, rivals, and students so no idea dies alone. The greatest taboo is building a machine that consumes people while pretending it only serves them, because that repeats the gods' own predatory logic. Ichor-touched Geisamahi may develop metallic whiskers, clock-tick heartbeats, sparks in their footprints, or an instinctive sense for cursed mechanisms. DM Hooks. Use their divine influence for tinker guilds, sewer scouts, arcane locksmiths, living machines, rival workshops, god-powered engines, or small inventors trying to keep Setrimir's stolen fire out of exploitative hands.

You are Small.; Speed. Your base walking speed is 30 feet. You also have a climbing speed of 30 feet.; Nimble Body. You can move through the space of any creature that is at least one size larger than you. Squeezing through spaces large enough for a Small creature costs you no extra movement.; Keen Whiskers and Nose. You gain proficiency in Perception or Investigation. You have advantage on checks made to locate hidden passages, traps, small objects, relics, food, scents, tracks, or recent disturbances in cluttered terrain.; Tinker-Claws. You gain proficiency with thieves' tools, tinkerer's tools, or one artisan's tool of your choice. During a short rest, you may improvise a tiny device, wedge, hook, noisemaker, trip-cord, patch, or simple mechanism from scavenged materials. The device lasts until your next long rest or until used.; Acrobatic Dash. As a bonus action, you may Dash, Disengage, or climb without provoking opportunity attacks until the end of your turn. races.label: Dragonborn — Noitzideq (Air and Weather)
races.description: parent dragons Asaafi + Sauqonsex, with Boisein storm influence; inherited theme Sky, weather, air/wind, storm movement, and healing currents.; profile Neutral Coordinator; scores Altruism 2000, Lawfulness 1650, Cooperation 2200, Honor 1850
races.pantheonInfluence: Valkhamesh and Nebyrr created the Dragonborn as scaled heirs of dragon parentage, sovereignty, storm-born dominion, lineage law, and dynastic memory. Creator God: Valkhamesh. Valkhamesh is honored as the creator of draconic bloodlines, sovereignty, storms, and ancient dominion. Dragonborn are not treated as a single uniform people; each lineage carries the mark of its dragon parentage, but the first divine ignition of draconic ancestry is traced to Valkhamesh's storm-bound authority. Scales, breath, wings, claws, and lineage instincts are read as living proof that ancient dominion still moves through mortal bodies. Secondary Divine Pressures. Nebyrr shapes Dragonborn inheritance, marriage law, dynasty records, oaths of bloodline legitimacy, and the legal status of mixed parentage. Enkirael influences war-clutches, conquest cults, honor-duels, and militant lineages that measure worth through victory. Horundar pulls oceanic, storm, volcanic, and pressure-bound lineages toward elemental extremes. Marduthor is revered by forge-scale clans that turn draconic anatomy into architecture, armor, and empire-building craft. Sigrananna influences forest, moonlit, green, and fey-adjacent dragonborn lineages that guard sacred groves or ecological pacts. Nefarokir governs funerary rites for dragonborn whose bloodlines remember the dead too strongly. Lineage Divine Use. A Dragonborn lineage can keep Valkhamesh as its creator-god while adding a patron pressure based on the parent dragons. Air, storm, and weather lineages often invoke Valkhamesh and Horundar together. Mountain, stone, crystal, and forge lineages often add Marduthor or Anubaldir. Ocean, tide, river, and reef lineages often add Bastveig or Horundar. Shadow, light, dream, and illusion lineages may add Raeshkul, Nephthysra, or Nefarokir depending on whether the culture frames the power as revelation, charisma, or liminal haunting. Rites, Taboos, and Ichor Marks. The Storm-Scale Naming is the most common birth rite: a hatchling or newly acknowledged Dragonborn is presented beneath open sky, near flame, stone, sea, or shadow according to lineage, and elders name the first dragon virtue seen in the child. The Bloodline Ledger is maintained by priests of Nebyrr so inheritance does not become mere conquest. A common taboo forbids claiming another Dragonborn's parentage without proof, because false bloodline claims are considered theft from Valkhamesh and fraud against Nebyrr. Ichor signs include storm-bright veins beneath the scales, breath that sparks before strong emotion, scale patterns resembling old territorial maps, and dreams of ancient wings over the world.
races.axisReading: Altruism: 1500 (Balanced empathy); Lawfulness: 2000 (Lawful); Cooperation: 1750 (Leaning cooperative); Honor: 2250 (Honorable).
races.canonTraitNames: Dragon Ancestry, Breath Weapon, Damage Resistance, Darkvision, Draconic Flight. Combined Ability Rule: A the source world Dragonborn gains the traditional Dragonborn trait package and the parentage features of its the source world dragon lineage. The breath, resistance, perception, and flight expressions remain active as standard draconic inheritance; the parentage features add bloodline-specific magic, senses, movement, survival, social, and elemental gifts. the source world Dragonborn Trait Framework: Ability Score Increase: Increase one ability score by 2 and another ability score by 1, or increase three different ability scores by 1 each.; Creature Type: You are a Humanoid with draconic ancestry.; Size: You are Medium.; Speed: Your base walking speed is 30 feet.; Darkvision: You can see in dim light within 60 feet as if it were bright light, and darkness as if it were dim light. You cannot discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.; Draconic Body: You have scaled skin, claws, a powerful tail, and facial ridges tied to your bloodline. races.pantheonInfluence: Valkhamesh and Nebyrr created the Dragonborn as scaled heirs of dragon parentage, sovereignty, storm-born dominion, lineage law, and dynastic memory. Creator God: Valkhamesh. Valkhamesh is honored as the creator of draconic bloodlines, sovereignty, storms, and ancient dominion. Dragonborn are not treated as a single uniform people; each lineage carries the mark of its dragon parentage, but the first divine ignition of draconic ancestry is traced to Valkhamesh's storm-bound authority. Scales, breath, wings, claws, and lineage instincts are read as living proof that ancient dominion still moves through mortal bodies. Secondary Divine Pressures. Nebyrr shapes Dragonborn inheritance, marriage law, dynasty records, oaths of bloodline legitimacy, and the legal status of mixed parentage. Enkirael influences war-clutches, conquest cults, honor-duels, and militant lineages that measure worth through victory. Horundar pulls oceanic, storm, volcanic, and pressure-bound lineages toward elemental extremes. Marduthor is revered by forge-scale clans that turn draconic anatomy into architecture, armor, and empire-building craft. Sigrananna influences forest, moonlit, green, and fey-adjacent dragonborn lineages that guard sacred groves or ecological pacts. Nefarokir governs funerary rites for dragonborn whose bloodlines remember the dead too strongly. Lineage Divine Use. A Dragonborn lineage can keep Valkhamesh as its creator-god while adding a patron pressure based on the parent dragons. Air, storm, and weather lineages often invoke Valkhamesh and Horundar together. Mountain, stone, crystal, and forge lineages often add Marduthor or Anubaldir. Ocean, tide, river, and reef lineages often add Bastveig or Horundar. Shadow, light, dream, and illusion lineages may add Raeshkul, Nephthysra, or Nefarokir depending on whether the culture frames the power as revelation, charisma, or liminal haunting. Rites, Taboos, and Ichor Marks. The Storm-Scale Naming is the most common birth rite: a hatchling or newly acknowledged Dragonborn is presented beneath open sky, near flame, stone, sea, or shadow according to lineage, and elders name the first dragon virtue seen in the child. The Bloodline Ledger is maintained by priests of Nebyrr so inheritance does not become mere conquest. A common taboo forbids claiming another Dragonborn's parentage without proof, because false bloodline claims are considered theft from Valkhamesh and fraud against Nebyrr. Ichor signs include storm-bright veins beneath the scales, breath that sparks before strong emotion, scale patterns resembling old territorial maps, and dreams of ancient wings over the world.

races.label: Aburata
races.description: Infernal Dual-Form Equinefolk of Ambition, Hellfire, and Commanding Presence.
races.lore: The Aburatas are a race of infernal beings . They possess two distinct forms that reflect their dual nature: a humanoid form and a quadrupedal, equine-inspired form. In humanoid form, Aburatas have polished, taut skin resembling obsidian, molten iron, or amethyst-violet, often etched with glowing sigils or ember-like vein patterns that pulse with their emotions. Their eyes blaze with infernal fire or sink into abyssal voids, and their hair can range from jet black to flame-red, silver-violet, or stark white. Horns emerge in unique shapes such as spiraled, antlered, or blade-like, glowing faintly with infernal energy, while a prehensile tail flickers with embers or faint hellfire, aiding balance and expressive gestures. In quadrupedal form, their humanoid upper bodies transition into powerful horse-like torsos sheathed in scaled textures reminiscent of volcanic stone or blackened steel, with muscular limbs ending in broad hooves that leave glowing, smoldering prints. The tail grows longer and more expressive, capable of grasping objects or assisting in movements, while the air around them carries heat and shadow, enhancing their imposing presence. Their voices are resonant and hypnotic, capable of commanding attention or inspiring unease. Aburatas are sustained by infernal energy rather than ordinary nourishment, drawing vitality from places of power, fire-lit areas, or sites infused with dark influence. They maintain stamina, focus, and resilience through sheer will and magical energy, and their infernal heritage grants them natural resistance to fire, curses, and corruption. Aburatas are highly charismatic, their presence amplifying social influence, persuasion, and intimidation. They exhibit keen dexterity and precision in both combat and manipulation of objects, aided by sharp, clawed hands in humanoid form.
races.pantheonInfluence: Secondary Divine Pressures. Enkirael influences Aburata war-herds and officer-cults, sharpening ambition into conquest, fury, and survival through dominance. Nephthysra influences salons, bloodline courts, and performers who turn charisma, beauty, and emotional command into social weapons. Nebyrr is invoked by noble Aburata houses whenever inheritance, marriage contracts, adoption, or dynastic succession must be legally sealed. Valkhamesh is respected by militant Aburata dynasties that frame command, cavalry, and storm-oath hierarchy as proof that power should flow downward from the strongest will. Rites, Taboos, and Ichor Marks. The Ember Crossroads Rite marks adulthood: an Aburata stands at a literal or symbolic crossroads and swears the first oath they are willing to pay for. The Bridle of the True Name is a private vow used by lovers, rivals, and war leaders to bind trust without surrendering autonomy. Breaking a bargained word is the worst taboo, because Aburata believe Freyseth hears every oath as food. Those strongly touched by divine ichor may develop black-glass veins, smoke-scented breath, or palm sigils that ache near contracts, curses, or imprisoned divine shrines. DM Hooks. Use Aburata pantheon influence to create infernal contract nobles, cavalry cults, oath-breaking fugitives, curse-lenders, or reformers trying to prove ambition does not have to become cruelty. A heroic Aburata can still carry Freyseth's hunger in their blood while choosing to make every bargain protective instead of predatory.

races.tableAbilities: Ability Score Increase. Your Charisma score increases by 2, and your Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution score increases by 1.; Creature Type. You are a Humanoid. You also count as a Fiend for prerequisites, spells, magical effects, or items that specifically affect fiendish creatures.; Size. You are Medium in humanoid form. In quadrupedal form, your body is still treated as Medium for normal play unless the DM rules a scene requires special handling.; Speed. Your base walking speed is 30 feet in humanoid form and 40 feet in quadrupedal form.; Dual Infernal Form. As a bonus action, you may shift between humanoid form and quadrupedal equine-inspired form. Your worn equipment merges, resizes, or remains worn as appropriate. In quadrupedal form, you cannot use equipment requiring two humanoid legs, but you gain advantage on ability checks made to run, carry, shove, resist being knocked prone, or traverse rough terrain.; Hellforged Resistance. You have resistance to fire damage. You have advantage on saving throws against curses, magical corruption, and effects that would frighten you.; Infernal Presence. You gain proficiency in Intimidation, Persuasion, Deception, or Performance. When you make a Charisma check against a creature that can see your horns, glowing sigils, ember-veins, or hellfire aura, you may add 1d4 to the roll. You can do so a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.; Horns, Tail, and Hooves. Your horns, prehensile tail, claws, or hooves are natural weapons. They deal 1d6 bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage. In quadrupedal form, your hooves may leave harmless smoldering prints and your carrying capacity counts as one size larger.; Infernal Spark. You know thaumaturgy. At 3rd level, you may cast hellish rebuke once per long rest. At 5th level, you may cast darkness or flaming sphere once per long rest. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells.; Languages. You can speak, read, and write Common and Infernal.

races.label: Volsarii
races.description: Four-Armed Ferriers of Souls, Liminal Balance, and Ethereal Wings.
races.lore: Volsariis are ethereal, multi-limbed beings . They possess four arms as a standard trait, elongated ears that curve upward and nearly resemble horns, and long, sensitive antennae atop their heads that detect changes in the environment, subtle emotions, and spiritual currents. Their skin ranges widely from iridescent shades of deep blues, greens, and storm-gray to luminous pastels, dawn-pinks, or shadowed violets, often streaked or veined with faint magical light, and may carry subtle markings that glow or shift with emotion, spiritual energy, or ambient magic. Their eyes vary from softly glowing gold, silver, and sky-blue to hollow voids, nebula-like patterns, or luminous starlight, reflecting both perception of the physical world and awareness of spirits, dream energy, or hidden currents. Hair flows lightly or appears almost weightless, with colors spanning metallic, pastel, starlit, or shadowed hues, sometimes giving the impression of liquid light, drifting mist, or feather-like strands. They maintain an elegant, deliberate grace in movement, capable of silent terrestrial motion, climbing, gliding, or, in their final life cycle, sprouting vast wings ranging from feathered to gossamer or ethereal forms, allowing them flight and aerial control that expresses both power and precision. Volsariis act as ferriers of the dead for Nyxarion, guiding souls through liminal spaces and maintaining the balance between life and death. They are attuned to both the waking and spiritual realms, able to sense, communicate with, and influence spirits, manage transitions, and preserve memory through subtle manipulation of energy, aura, or pheromones. Their abilities blend ethereal perception, dream- or shadow-influenced magic, and radiant or elemental powers, allowing them to phase through matter, weave illusions, manipulate light, wind, or celestial energies, and project calming, inspiring, or disorienting auras. Rituals, meditation, and communion with sacred or magical sites restore vitality, while harsh, chaotic, or energy-depleted environments can diminish focus and magical resonance. Volsariis draw sustenance primarily from ambient magic, spiritual energy, or dream currents rather than conventional food, though symbolic consumption may accompany ceremonial practices. Their culture emphasizes cycles, reflection, guardianship, guidance, and balance, blending artistic expression, dreamwork, and ritual observances with precise attention to the flow of life, death, and magical currents.
races.pantheonInfluence: Creator God: Nefarokir. Nefarokir is the primary creator of the Volsarii, making them four-armed ferriers of souls, liminal balance keepers, spiritual witnesses, and guides through the passage between life and death. Their bodies are understood as living thresholds: two hands may comfort the living while two hands hold the path open for the dead. Secondary Divine Pressures. Nebyrr is invoked by funerary houses, inheritance courts, marriage archives, and lineage keepers who need death to be legally and socially recognized. Sokhivar is sung to by winged Volsarii in their final life-cycle, especially when sunlight, prophecy, music, and aerial freedom guide souls toward the next horizon. Raeshkul influences memory-keepers and psychic mourners who preserve testimony from both sides of death. Eirzunet is feared in shadow passages where a soul can be transformed, hidden, or cursed before it reaches proper accounting. Hathruna is honored by Volsarii who emphasize rebirth, composted grief, and the renewal that follows mourning. Rites, Taboos, and Ichor Marks. The Four Hands Passing is the central funerary rite: one hand closes the eyes, one records the name, one comforts the living, and one gestures toward the unseen road. The Wingwake marks the final life-cycle of a Volsarii whose wings have emerged, often transforming them into honored guides, prophets, or terrifying omens. Abandoning a soul for payment, falsifying a death record, or trapping grief for power are grave taboos. Ichor-touched Volsarii may cast wing-shaped shadows before wings grow, hear clocks stop near the dying, or see black threads connecting the living to unresolved deaths. DM Hooks. Use Volsarii pantheon influence for soul-ferry guilds, industrial death ledgers, funeral courts, prophetic winged elders, memory disputes, escaped souls, or Nefarokir cults trying to turn ferriers into collectors.

You are Medium.; Speed. Your base walking speed is 30 feet.; Four Arms. You have four arms. The secondary pair can hold objects, perform somatic components, open doors, carry tools, or interact with items. They do not grant extra attacks, additional shields, or extra two-handed weapon use unless the DM allows a specific feature to do so.; Antennae and Spirit Senses. You gain proficiency in Insight, Perception, or Religion. You have advantage on checks made to notice emotional shifts, spiritual residue, undead presence, or changes in magical atmosphere.; Ferrier of the Dead. You know spare the dying. At 3rd level, you may cast protection from evil and good once per long rest. At 5th level, you may cast gentle repose or augury once per long rest. Wisdom or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells.; Liminal Step. As a bonus action, you may become partially ethereal until the end of your turn. During this movement, you may move through the space of creatures and ignore nonmagical difficult terrain. If you end your turn inside an object, you are shunted to the nearest open space and take force damage equal to your level. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.; Winged Final Cycle. Your wings begin as spiritual, feathered, gossamer, or ethereal structures. When you fall, you may use your reaction to glide and reduce falling damage by five times your level. At 5th level, you may fly for 1 minute at a speed of 30 feet once per long rest.; Languages. You can speak, read, and write Common and one language associated with spirits, celestial courts, shadow realms, or ancestral rites.

races.label: Gandirosha
races.description: Luck-Touched Wanderers of Charm, Timing, and Subtle Magic.
races.lore: Gandiroshas are a race of magical, agile beings . Their presence in the source world is defined by charm, intuition, and a deep attunement to both chance and the subtle flows of magic in their environment. They range from petite to tall, standing between three and six feet, with wiry or lithe builds suited to quick movement, climbing, and graceful gestures. Their skin carries a natural, faint glow that can take the form of star-like freckles, soft sigils, or flowing patterns that shift with emotion, magical activity, or sunlight. Hair ranges from honey and chestnut to copper, gold, and jade tones, often styled in flowing waves, curls, or dramatic braids, adorned with charms, beads, or small enchanted trinkets that reflect personal flair and magical presence. Eyes are expressive and varied, including amber, hazel, deep brown, gold, green, or soft blue, capable of subtle luminescence when Gandiroshas focus their magical or intuitive senses. Their clothing blends practicality with artistry, often layered, flowing, or accented with pouches, charms, and symbols, allowing both freedom of movement and the display of individual style. Gandiroshas possess an innate connection to luck, opportunity, and the hidden currents of events around them, allowing them to sense favorable outcomes, detect subtle threats, and influence social or magical situations through intuition, charm, and clever timing. They move with remarkable lightness and agility, slipping past obstacles, navigating crowded spaces, or disappearing briefly from sight with fleeting illusions or environmental blending. Their social skills are heightened, drawing vitality and focus from interaction, shared meals, stories, music, or companionship, while isolation, stress, or chaotic surroundings can diminish their magical acuity. Gandiroshas have finely tuned perception, enabling them to read intentions, uncover hidden treasures, detect traps, and anticipate outcomes with uncanny accuracy. Their subtle magic can influence luck, create brief illusions, manipulate small objects, or enhance group morale through presence and charisma.
races.pantheonInfluence: Creator God: Thalunesh. Thalunesh is the primary creator of the Gandirosha, filling them with luck-touched movement, charming mischief, wanderer instincts, and subtle timing magic. Their culture teaches that luck is not random: it is a moving door, and a clever soul learns when to step through before the lock remembers it is closed. Secondary Divine Pressures. Asethyr shapes their revels, road festivals, tribal games, and wild ceremonies where freedom is treated as a sacred survival skill. Nephthysra influences performers, courtiers, and social gamblers who use beauty, emotion, and charm to redirect danger before swords are drawn. Nebyrr is a favorite target and reluctant patron, because Gandirosha often survive by learning lineage laws, travel permits, inheritance loopholes, and marriage customs well enough to bend them. Eirzunet haunts cursed tricks, shadow wagers, false faces, and jokes that become transformations. Rites, Taboos, and Ichor Marks. The Turning Coin Rite is performed before major journeys: a coin, shell, or knucklebone is tossed, but the initiate is judged by how they respond after the result rather than by which side lands upward. The Roadmask Festival allows every participant to lie for one night, but only to reveal a truth by dawn. The greatest taboo is stealing another person's future by tricking them into a bargain they could not understand. Ichor-touched Gandirosha may hear dice before danger, cast the wrong shadow, or briefly see three possible outcomes reflected in mirrors. DM Hooks. Their pantheon ties make Gandirosha ideal as prophetic gamblers, caravan tricksters, oath-law hackers, fey couriers, masked rebels, or cursed comedians whose jokes accidentally open divine doors.

races.tableAbilities: Ability Score Increase. Your Dexterity score increases by 2, and your Charisma, Wisdom, or Intelligence score increases by 1.; Creature Type. You are a Humanoid.; Size. You are Small or Medium, chosen when selecting this race.; Speed. Your base walking speed is 30 feet.; Fortune Sense. You gain proficiency in Insight, Perception, Sleight of Hand, or Persuasion. You also have advantage on ability checks made to notice traps, hidden valuables, loaded dice, false smiles, or subtle shifts in social mood.; Lucky Timing. When you fail an ability check, attack roll, or saving throw, you may roll 1d4 and add it to the result, potentially turning failure into success. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus and regain all expended uses after a long rest.; Fleeting Glamour. You know minor illusion. Starting at 3rd level, you may cast disguise self once per long rest. Starting at 5th level, you may cast invisibility once per long rest, targeting only yourself. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells.; Lightfoot Agility. You can move through the space of a creature that is at least one size larger than you. You also ignore nonmagical difficult terrain caused by crowds, clutter, loose rubble, market stalls, furniture, or narrow urban spaces.; Communal Spark. During a short rest, if you share food, music, storytelling, games, or friendly conversation with at least one ally, you and one creature who joined you gain temporary hit points equal to your proficiency bonus.; Languages. You can speak, read, and write Common and one additional language of your choice.

races.label: Panolima — Earth Thread
races.description: Panolima Earth Thread embodies stone, soil, grounding force, caves, and earth-aligned ritual places.
races.lore: The Panolimas are beings of elemental harmony . Their bodies are infused with one of the five primordial elemental threads: Earth, Fire, Water, Air, or Aether. Each individual exhibits physical traits reflecting their elemental affinity, from stone-like skin and mossy hair to flowing, water-like forms or luminous, energy-filled auras. They thrive in environments aligned with their element, drawing sustenance, vitality, and energy from landscapes, currents, storms, magma, or ley lines. Their movements, gestures, and even voices often carry the rhythm of their element, and they engage in ritual cleansing or meditation to maintain harmony with their elemental thread. Earth Panolimas have skin patterned like bark or stone, hair resembling moss or soil, and a deep-toned, rumbling voice. They require contact with solid terrain, forests, caves, or mountains to maintain vitality. Their abilities include sensing structural weaknesses, reinforcing the land, and enduring physical hardships with exceptional resilience. They can read terrain, detect mineral-rich soils, and manipulate stone or plant life to shape their surroundings. Fire Panolimas exhibit cracks like magma across their skin, ember-red hair, and glowing eyes. They rely on heat sources, volcanic activity, and exposure to flames to sustain energy. Their bodies radiate warmth and light, and they can manipulate molten materials, summon bursts of flame, and purify areas through fire.
races.pantheonInfluence: Creator God: Horundar. Horundar is the primary creator of the Panolima, whose elemental threads of earth, fire, water, air, and aether embody the unstable boundaries of ocean, storm, pressure, and upheaval. Panolima do not merely use elements; they are living negotiations between forces that would otherwise break the world apart. Secondary Divine Pressures. Oskar'enlil studies Panolima balance as a living experiment in civilization, instinct, elemental pressure, and structured survival. Bastveig influences Water Panolima who treat currents and reefs as living memory. Marduthor appears among Fire and Earth Panolima who turn heat, stone, and metal into craft. Sigrananna shapes plant-rich Earth and Air communities through wilderness harmony, while Valkhamesh influences storm-born Panolima who see hierarchy in lightning and pressure. Elemental Influence Notes. Earth Panolima often honor Anubaldir, Marduthor, or Sigrananna depending on whether their culture emphasizes burden, craft, or roots. Fire Panolima may honor Marduthor's forge or Enkirael's battle-flame, creating a major ethical divide. Water Panolima most often answer Horundar and Bastveig together. Air Panolima add Sokhivar for song, prophecy, and sky freedom. Aether Panolima are frequently watched by Raeshkul and Oskar'enlil because their bodies suggest that elements can become thought, law, and living theory. Rites, Taboos, and Ichor Marks. The Fivefold Stillness requires a Panolima to sit within the presence of all five threads and refuse to let any single element dominate the others. Elemental hoarding is taboo: a Panolima who uses their thread to destroy the balance that sustains others is treated as spiritually starving. Ichor-touched Panolima may leak black steam, carry glassy fault-lines in the skin, hear storms before clouds form, or lose control of one element whenever a divine prison nearby hungers.

races.label: Gwynis
races.description: Dream-Born Ethereals of Illusion, Memory, and Psychic Insight.
races.lore: Gwynises are ethereal, dream-born beings . Their appearances range widely, from tall, slender, shadow-touched figures to luminous, starlit forms with flowing, weightless hair and shifting, aurora-like or mist-like skin patterns that reflect thought, emotion, or ambient magical energy. Eyes vary from glowing moons and crystalline orbs to hollow voids or softly luminescent shades, capable of perceiving layers of reality, psychic echoes, or dreamscapes. Their bodies can phase between tangible and ghostly states, trailing wisps, shadowed tendrils, or dreamlike distortions that ripple with their movements, and their fingers and limbs are long, dexterous, and capable of absorbing mana, manipulating subtle forces, or projecting dream energy. Gwynises move with fluid grace and silent precision, able to influence perception, subtly manipulate emotion, or weave ephemeral illusions and constructs from thought, dream, and psychic resonance. They thrive in magical, artistic, or low-light environments, sustaining themselves through dream energy, meditation, ambient magic, or symbolic nourishment, while chaotic or harsh surroundings can diminish focus, well-being, and psychic attunement. Gwynises possess a versatile range of abilities that blend ethereal grace, dreamcraft, and subtle guardianship. They can obscure themselves, manipulate perception, cloud memory, or guide and protect others through psychic insight and dream influence. They are capable of lucid dreamcraft, weaving illusions, threading thought into reality, and sensing hidden truths or intentions in both waking and dream realms. Their physical and metaphysical forms are resilient, enduring environmental extremes while maintaining grace, or phasing through matter and shadows when needed. Some Gwynises manifest ephemeral or surreal adornments, levitating objects, flowing tattoos, or subtle elemental or celestial effects that mirror their inner state. They can influence emotion and perception through presence, pheromones, or vocal resonance, and their aura often bends reality subtly around them, inspiring awe, creativity, or reflection in observers.
races.pantheonInfluence: Creator God: Raeshkul. Raeshkul is the primary creator of the Gwynis, shaping their dream-born bodies around psychic insight, memory, illusion, and higher understanding. Their minds are treated as temples without walls: every dream, memory, and false image can become a corridor leading toward strategy, revelation, or danger. Secondary Divine Pressures. Eirzunet haunts Gwynis dream-shadows, forbidden transformations, and nightmares that teach too much. Thalunesh influences wandering dreamers, playful illusions, and the luck of impossible timing. Nefarokir is present when Gwynis preserve the memories of the dead or receive dreams from souls that should have passed on. Sokhivar touches prophetic music, sunlight visions, and winged dream-symbols that guide a seer toward the next horizon. Rites, Taboos, and Ichor Marks. The Mirror-Sleep Rite requires a Gwynis to sleep beside a covered mirror, then uncover it at dawn and describe which part of the self did not return. Memory-braiding is a communal practice where several Gwynis share one important recollection so grief, strategy, or prophecy cannot be erased by a single death. Invading a mind for curiosity alone is a taboo, while erasing grief without consent is treated as spiritual murder. Ichor-touched Gwynis may bleed ink-dark tears, speak in layered voices while dreaming, or carry floating memory motes visible in moonlight. DM Hooks. Their pantheon influence supports psychic diplomats, dream spies, memory archivists, illusionist rebels, nightmare-cursed oracles, and communities targeted by gods who want their secrets back.

races.tableAbilities: Ability Score Increase. Increase your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma score by 2, and increase one other ability score by 1.; Creature Type. You are a Humanoid. You also count as a Fey for prerequisites, spells, magical effects, or items that specifically affect fey creatures.; Size. You are Small or Medium, chosen when selecting this race.; Speed. Your base walking speed is 30 feet.; Dreamsight. You have darkvision out to 60 feet. While in dim light, darkness, dreams, magical mist, or an illusion, you can tell whether a creature within 30 feet is awake, asleep, frightened, charmed, or under an illusion, unless that creature is protected by magic that blocks divination.; Lucid Dreamcraft. You know minor illusion. At 3rd level, you may cast silent image once per long rest. At 5th level, you may cast phantasmal force or calm emotions once per long rest. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells, chosen when selecting this race.; Ethereal Flicker. As a reaction when you take damage, you may partially phase. Reduce the damage by an amount equal to your proficiency bonus + the modifier of your chosen spellcasting ability. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.; Memory Threader. You gain proficiency in Insight, Performance, Persuasion, or Stealth. You have advantage on checks made to interpret symbolism, dreams, artistic metaphors, emotional echoes, or psychic impressions.; Dream Rest. You do not sleep in the ordinary way. During a long rest, you enter a lucid meditative dream for 4 hours while remaining dimly aware of your surroundings.; Languages. You can speak, read, and write Common and Sylvan or one language tied to dream, spirit, or arcane traditions.

races.label: Deorbasun — Hunter Instinct
races.description: Deorbasun Hunter Instinct favors stalking, territorial patrols, forests, grasslands, and wild hunting grounds.
races.lore: Deorbasuns are majestic. Their physiques range from muscular, feline-like frames to lithe, agile forms with fur, scales, or earth-toned skin, reflecting a deep connection to predatory grace, wilderness instinct, and mystical energy. Heights vary widely, from six to nine feet, and their limbs are long and flexible, ending in retractable claws or talons capable of channeling energy or venom. Eyes glow with intelligence and authority, displaying hues from ember and gold to crystalline blues, greens, or silver, and often carry faint luminescence that responds to magic or emotion. Hair and manes vary from obsidian black, smoldering crimson, and radiant gold to bioluminescent strands, shimmered locks, or ethereal highlights, often adorned with beads, feathers, bones, or gemstones marking achievements, lineage, or ritual significance. Wings, tails, or subtle soul-animal traits enhance both presence and ability, with wings capable of flight or generating gusts, tails delivering venom, radiant energy, or prehensile utility, and faint ethereal markings or patterns tying form to instinct and magic. Deorbasuns possess extraordinary physical and magical abilities that blend predatory skill, shapeshifting versatility, and environmental attunement. They can leap with precision, maneuver through air or terrain with grace, and strike with claws, fangs, or tails imbued with energy or venom. Some can shift subtly to reflect traits of a soul-animal, such as enhanced senses, agility, or elemental affinities, while others maintain a consistently imposing, feline-like or beastly form. Their endurance and stamina are exceptional, allowing them to traverse rugged terrain, hunt, or perform ritualized movement for extended periods. They absorb energy through magical currents, prey, or ambient mana, and their focus and vitality are renewed through hunting, meditation, ritual exposure, or communion with natural and mystical environments. Deorbasuns are highly perceptive, capable of reading subtle environmental cues, sensing magical disturbances, and coordinating with wildlife or allies in ways that reflect both strategic intelligence and instinctual response.
races.pantheonInfluence: Creator God: Iskareth. Iskareth is the primary creator of the Deorbasun, shaping their beast-souled bodies from instinct, fertility, natural kinship, and guardian grace. Their soul-animal traits are understood as divine fragments of Iskareth's first wilderness memory: claw, wing, fang, horn, hide, and watchful eye each represent a sacred duty to defend territory without severing kinship with the living world. Secondary Divine Pressures. Anubaldir is honored by territorial guardians who treat endurance and burden as inherited obligations rather than personal virtues. Asethyr influences revels, hunt-feasts, and tribal rites where wilderness freedom becomes sacred survival. Nebyrr appears in boundary law, marriage bonds between guardian clans, and formal oaths that decide who may pass through protected territory. Sigrananna is invoked by moonlit forest Deorbasun, especially those who guard elven groves, old roads, or sacred beasts. Rites, Taboos, and Ichor Marks. The Boundary Vigil sends young Deorbasun to walk the edge of a chosen territory for one full night without speaking, learning where duty ends and domination begins. The First Hunt is not a kill-trial, but a restraint-trial: the initiate must prove they can track, judge, and spare when the land does not require blood. Wasting prey, abandoning a sworn boundary, or hunting only for vanity are deep taboos. Ichor-touched Deorbasun may show glowing paw-print markings, stone-heavy bones, prophetic animal dreams, or a voice that quiets frightened beasts. DM Hooks. Their divine culture supports shrine guardians, border wardens, sacred beast judges, territorial paladins, cursed exiles, or clans divided between Iskareth's kinship and Enkirael's domination. A Deorbasun antagonist does not need to be evil: they may simply believe the party has crossed a boundary the gods themselves once marked.
races.axisReading: Altruism: 1800: Skewed Altruistic - How strongly the race tends toward care, protection, generosity, or self-interest.; Lawfulness: 1750: Skewed Lawful - How strongly the race tends toward rules, ritual, hierarchy, contracts, or freedom from structure.; Cooperation: 1500: Balanced / Neutral - How strongly the race tends toward shared work, communal life, party loyalty, or lone methods.; Honor: 2250: Extreme Honorable - How strongly the race tends toward vows, truth, restraint, internal codes, or ruthless pragmatism.
races.tableAbilities: Ability Score Increase. Your Strength or Dexterity score increases by 2, and your Wisdom or Charisma score increases by 1.; Creature Type. You are a Humanoid.; Size. You are Medium. Many Deorbasuns stand between six and nine feet tall, but your playable size remains Medium.; Speed. Your base walking speed is 35 feet.; Predatory Natural Weapons. Your claws, fangs, talons, horns, or tail are natural weapons. When you hit with an unarmed strike, you may deal slashing, piercing, or bludgeoning damage equal to 1d6 + your Strength or Dexterity modifier.; Soul-Animal Instinct. Choose one instinct when selecting this race: Hunter, Guardian, Winged, Venomtail, or Mystic. Hunter grants proficiency in Stealth or Survival. Guardian grants proficiency in Intimidation or Athletics. Winged grants the Winged Maneuver trait below. Venomtail lets your natural weapon deal poison damage instead of its normal type once per turn. Mystic grants proficiency in Arcana, Nature, or Religion.; Ritual Hunt. Once per long rest, as a bonus action, you mark one creature you can see for 1 minute. The first time each turn you hit the marked creature with an attack, you deal extra damage equal to your proficiency bonus. This damage type matches your natural weapon or a magical energy associated with your soul-animal.; Winged Maneuver. If you chose the Winged instinct, your wings allow brief aerial control. When you jump or fall, you may glide up to 20 feet horizontally and reduce falling damage by an amount equal to five times your level.; Territorial Awareness. You have advantage on Wisdom (Perception or Survival) checks made to track creatures, sense intruders, identify disturbed terrain, or notice magical disturbances in your claimed territory or current campsite.; Languages. You can speak, read, and write Common and one additional language of your choice.

races.description: Deorbasun Mystic Instinct favors sacred groves, ritual territories, spirit-haunted wilds, and magical boundary lands.
races.lore: Deorbasuns are majestic. Their physiques range from muscular, feline-like frames to lithe, agile forms with fur, scales, or earth-toned skin, reflecting a deep connection to predatory grace, wilderness instinct, and mystical energy. Heights vary widely, from six to nine feet, and their limbs are long and flexible, ending in retractable claws or talons capable of channeling energy or venom. Eyes glow with intelligence and authority, displaying hues from ember and gold to crystalline blues, greens, or silver, and often carry faint luminescence that responds to magic or emotion. Hair and manes vary from obsidian black, smoldering crimson, and radiant gold to bioluminescent strands, shimmered locks, or ethereal highlights, often adorned with beads, feathers, bones, or gemstones marking achievements, lineage, or ritual significance. Wings, tails, or subtle soul-animal traits enhance both presence and ability, with wings capable of flight or generating gusts, tails delivering venom, radiant energy, or prehensile utility, and faint ethereal markings or patterns tying form to instinct and magic. Deorbasuns possess extraordinary physical and magical abilities that blend predatory skill, shapeshifting versatility, and environmental attunement. They can leap with precision, maneuver through air or terrain with grace, and strike with claws, fangs, or tails imbued with energy or venom. Some can shift subtly to reflect traits of a soul-animal, such as enhanced senses, agility, or elemental affinities, while others maintain a consistently imposing, feline-like or beastly form. Their endurance and stamina are exceptional, allowing them to traverse rugged terrain, hunt, or perform ritualized movement for extended periods. They absorb energy through magical currents, prey, or ambient mana, and their focus and vitality are renewed through hunting, meditation, ritual exposure, or communion with natural and mystical environments. Deorbasuns are highly perceptive, capable of reading subtle environmental cues, sensing magical disturbances, and coordinating with wildlife or allies in ways that reflect both strategic intelligence and instinctual response.
races.pantheonInfluence: Creator God: Iskareth. Iskareth is the primary creator of the Deorbasun, shaping their beast-souled bodies from instinct, fertility, natural kinship, and guardian grace. Their soul-animal traits are understood as divine fragments of Iskareth's first wilderness memory: claw, wing, fang, horn, hide, and watchful eye each represent a sacred duty to defend territory without severing kinship with the living world. Secondary Divine Pressures. Anubaldir is honored by territorial guardians who treat endurance and burden as inherited obligations rather than personal virtues. Asethyr influences revels, hunt-feasts, and tribal rites where wilderness freedom becomes sacred survival. Nebyrr appears in boundary law, marriage bonds between guardian clans, and formal oaths that decide who may pass through protected territory. Sigrananna is invoked by moonlit forest Deorbasun, especially those who guard elven groves, old roads, or sacred beasts. Rites, Taboos, and Ichor Marks. The Boundary Vigil sends young Deorbasun to walk the edge of a chosen territory for one full night without speaking, learning where duty ends and domination begins. The First Hunt is not a kill-trial, but a restraint-trial: the initiate must prove they can track, judge, and spare when the land does not require blood. Wasting prey, abandoning a sworn boundary, or hunting only for vanity are deep taboos. Ichor-touched Deorbasun may show glowing paw-print markings, stone-heavy bones, prophetic animal dreams, or a voice that quiets frightened beasts. DM Hooks. Their divine culture supports shrine guardians, border wardens, sacred beast judges, territorial paladins, cursed exiles, or clans divided between Iskareth's kinship and Enkirael's domination. A Deorbasun antagonist does not need to be evil: they may simply believe the party has crossed a boundary the gods themselves once marked.

You are Medium. Many Deorbasuns stand between six and nine feet tall, but your playable size remains Medium.; Speed. Your base walking speed is 35 feet.; Predatory Natural Weapons. Your claws, fangs, talons, horns, or tail are natural weapons. When you hit with an unarmed strike, you may deal slashing, piercing, or bludgeoning damage equal to 1d6 + your Strength or Dexterity modifier.; Soul-Animal Instinct. Choose one instinct when selecting this race: Hunter, Guardian, Winged, Venomtail, or Mystic. Hunter grants proficiency in Stealth or Survival. Guardian grants proficiency in Intimidation or Athletics. Winged grants the Winged Maneuver trait below. Venomtail lets your natural weapon deal poison damage instead of its normal type once per turn. Mystic grants proficiency in Arcana, Nature, or Religion.; Ritual Hunt. Once per long rest, as a bonus action, you mark one creature you can see for 1 minute. The first time each turn you hit the marked creature with an attack, you deal extra damage equal to your proficiency bonus. This damage type matches your natural weapon or a magical energy associated with your soul-animal.; Winged Maneuver. If you chose the Winged instinct, your wings allow brief aerial control. When you jump or fall, you may glide up to 20 feet horizontally and reduce falling damage by an amount equal to five times your level.; Territorial Awareness. You have advantage on Wisdom (Perception or Survival) checks made to track creatures, sense intruders, identify disturbed terrain, or notice magical disturbances in your claimed territory or current campsite.; Languages. You can speak, read, and write Common and one additional language of your choice.

races.label: Dril'thar — Grassland Lineage
races.description: Rain-fed grassland and hidden wetland Dril'thar suited to plains, prairie waterholes, and seasonal pools.
races.lore: The Dril'thar are an ancient amphibious people whose civilizations rise from swamps, flooded jungles, coral reefs, mangrove coasts, subterranean rivers, mist-choked marshes, and sacred rainforests. Across countless regions of the world, they are known as healers, navigators, mystics, hunters, survivalists, and wandering pilgrims capable of thriving where most civilizations would collapse. To outsiders, Dril'thar are often misunderstood as poisonous frogfolk, territorial swamp-creatures, or eerie marsh spirits. In truth, they are one of the most biologically adaptable and spiritually complex peoples in existence. Their philosophy teaches that all things move in cycles: rain becomes river, river becomes sea, decay becomes renewal, and death feeds life anew. Water is not merely an element to the Dril'thar—it is memory, ancestry, spirit, and destiny itself. A spawning pool may serve simultaneously as temple, cemetery, and place of prophecy, for the Dril'thar believe the currents of the world carry the echoes of those who came before.
races.pantheonInfluence: Creator God: Bastveig. Bastveig is the primary creator of the Dril'thar, binding amphibious mysticism, reef stewardship, hydromancy, and living water memory into their bodies. Dril'thar spawning pools are not only places of birth, but divine archives: their water is believed to remember every ancestor, every flood, every drowning, and every bargain made with the deep. Secondary Divine Pressures. Thoryn-Rahek appears in mutation myths, especially among lineages whose bodies adapt too quickly or in ways that feel alien even to other Dril'thar. Hathruna shapes marsh, rot, and renewal traditions where decay feeds pools and pools feed new life. Horundar influences ocean, storm, and flood clans who believe catastrophe can purify stagnant civilizations. Nefarokir is present in gravewater rites, where pools serve as cemeteries, memory wells, and thresholds for souls who died in water. Lineage Influence Notes. Grassland Dril'thar often honor Ishtanora for rain-fed survival and hidden wetland gardens. Swamp and marsh lineages commonly invoke Hathruna and Nefarokir together, treating rot and death as two halves of the same sacred current. Rainforest and forest lineages add Sigrananna to Bastveig's rites, while reef and ocean lineages are the most direct inheritors of Bastveig's deep-water civilization. Mutated or unusually colored children may be protected, feared, or consecrated depending on whether the clan reads the sign as Bastveig's blessing or Thoryn-Rahek's echo. Rites, Taboos, and Ichor Marks. The Pool of Names ceremony lets a clan recite its dead into living water so the next generation can dream them. The Tide Confession requires a Dril'thar to speak secrets into flowing water rather than into stone, because stillness traps guilt. Polluting a birth-pool, damming ancestral water without consent, or draining a cemetery-marsh are treated as sacrilege. Ichor-touched Dril'thar may develop black bioluminescent freckles, prophetic mucus patterns, voices that ripple water, or mutations that bloom after divine dreams.
